Consider the vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}: \mathbb{R}^{4} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^2$ defined by
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217875/assets/2e7f8144a8cb560911b65d4ca657148df69568184b1aca0e89b5551e0d3cdcae.svg)

What is $\dfrac{\textrm{d} \mathbf{f}}{\textrm{d} \mathbf{x}},$ the total derivative of $\mathbf{f}$ with respect to $\mathbf{x}$ at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217875/assets/adccb3fb0692529551c254d01387a1c1950ff044def046da83d1331fd9271ea1.svg)
question.worked_solution:
The total derivative of a vector-valued function $\mathbf{f}: \mathbb{R}^{n} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^m$ with respect to a vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ is the $m \times n$ matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217875/assets/01a79963b1871d82fdd7244b67eb2185cd9bc3e1f066d0def6366552677b32fe.svg)

In our case, writing out the function $\mathbf{f}(\mathbf{x})$ where ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217875/assets/f621db9742637aa006cc2033c77d6d30cf664529fd94cc2db9964effa2c44ed5.svg), we get
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217875/assets/4825869f62821be4a775d58c7e85c03948025be018489cabb460156f74d80a58.svg)

From here, we have $f_1(\mathbf{x}) = x_1 + 2x_2 + 4x_3 + 8x_4$ and $f_2(\mathbf{x}) = x_1 + 3x_2 + 9x_3 +27x_4.$ So, the total derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}\,\,\,\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =[\begin{aligned}\frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{3}} & \frac{∂{f}_{1}}{∂{x}_{4}} \\ \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{1}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{2}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{3}} & \frac{∂{f}_{2}}{∂{x}_{4}}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 2 & 4 & 8 \\ 1 & 3 & 9 & 27\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

Since the total derivative is a constant matrix, evaluating it at ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14217875/assets/5001c288fe848bed80ed10055323aad27c90d0acab2088baf9fc48ebe17b3f4a.svg) gives the same matrix.
